sentences.text: The type specimen of Changchengornis is smaller than the smallest known specimens of its relative Confuciusornis.
The deltopectoral crest of the humerus in Changchengornis is not pierced.
The holotype GMV-2129 displays two elongated, ribbon-like tail feathers similar to those found in male Confuciusornis specimens.
The fossil suggests the presence of a head tuft or crest that would resemble modern turacos, though this feature might be an artifact of conservation.
In 1998, researchers Ji Shuan and Luis Chiappe identified a specimen of Confuciusornis that appeared distinct from others in the National Geological Museum of China.
In 1999, Ji, Chiappe, and Ji Qiang formally named the species Changchengornis hengdaoziensis.
The holotype specimen GMV-2129 was discovered near the village of Jianshangou in Liaoning province within the Jianshangou Beds of the Hengdaozi Member.
The holotype consists of a largely complete, articulated, but compressed and damaged skeleton preserved as a plate and counterplate.
In 1999, Changchengornis was assigned to the family Confuciusornithidae.
Remains of Changchengornis have been found in the Chaomidianzi Formation in China, dating to the Barremian-Aptian boundary approximately 125 million years ago.
The time range for Changchengornis is the Barremian to Aptian, spanning from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
